channel.title: n8n release notes: editor and nodes
channel.description: Feature-level updates from n8n releases: what shipped in the editor and the integration nodes.

item.title: Add agent card chat preview action
item.description: Agent cards in the Agents list now include a dedicated New Chat icon button, replacing the option previously buried in the card's overflow menu. Clicking it opens the agent builder with the preview panel already visible and immediately starts a new chat session, making it faster to test an agent.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add the chat member get many operation
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node now supports a new Chat Member resource with a Get Many operation, letting users list the members of an existing chat via a chat picker, with optional limits or return-all pagination. This works with delegated OAuth2 credentials; since the chat picker cannot list chats under a Service Principal (app-only) credential, the resource's operation and fields are hidden with an explanatory notice in that case.

item.title: GraphQL Node: Add support for predefined credential types
item.description: The GraphQL node's Authentication dropdown now includes a "Predefined Credential Type" option, matching the HTTP Request node. Users can select from n8n's built-in credential types (such as GitHub API or Slack API) instead of manually re-entering auth details, making it easier to connect GraphQL endpoints for services n8n already supports.

item.title: Add progress feedback to the artifact panel while the AI Assistant builds
item.description: The AI Assistant's artifact panel now shows live progress while the assistant is building or editing an agent or workflow. A floating 'AI Assistant is making changes…' indicator appears over the agent preview, and spinners replace the icon on the affected artifact tab and sidebar row, so the panel feels connected to the chat instead of appearing idle mid-build. Indicators clear automatically once the change completes.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add get and reply operations for channel messages
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node's Channel Message resource now supports three new operations: Get (fetch a single message by ID), Reply (post a threaded reply to an existing message), and Get Many Replies (list replies with pagination support). Replying is now a discoverable, dedicated action usable by AI agents, rather than a hidden option inside Create. Existing workflows using the old Reply to ID field continue to work unchanged. Create and Reply remain unavailable with Service Principal credentials, since app-only Graph access can't post channel messages.

item.title: Confluence Node: Add Atlassian Service Account (2LO) authentication
item.description: The Confluence node now supports authenticating via an Atlassian Service Account (2LO) credential, alongside the existing Cloud OAuth2 option. A new Authentication selector lets you choose which credential to use, with all API calls, binary downloads, uploads, site selection, and caching routed accordingly. Existing workflows without the selector default to Cloud OAuth2, so behavior is unchanged.

item.title: Jira Node: Add Atlassian Service Account (2LO) authentication
item.description: The Jira node now supports Atlassian Service Account authentication (OAuth 2.0 client credentials, 2LO) as a new 'Cloud (Service Account)' option alongside existing Cloud, Cloud OAuth2, Server, and Server PAT modes. Service accounts don't consume a Jira license seat and remain usable after employee offboarding. Existing credentials and workflows are unaffected. A related core fix prevents corrupted file uploads by avoiding replay of already-sent stream/form-data bodies after a token refresh.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add Online Meeting Get operation
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node's Online Meeting resource now supports a Get operation. Users can retrieve a meeting by its ID or by its join URL, using a single Meeting resource locator parameter. Lookups by URL query Microsoft Graph's onlineMeetings filter, while ID lookups fetch the meeting directly, with clearer error messages when a meeting can't be found.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add Online Meeting resource with Create operation
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node now supports a new Online Meeting resource with a Create operation, letting you schedule Teams meetings with subject, start/end times, and optional settings like lobby bypass, meeting chat mode, presenter permissions, recording, and passcode. This requires an OAuth2 credential (reconnect existing ones to grant the new OnlineMeetings.ReadWrite scope); the feature is unavailable with Service Principal credentials.

item.title: Databricks Node: Send a partner User-Agent on every API call
item.description: The Databricks node now sends a partner User-Agent (n8n_DatabricksNode/1.0) on every API call and credential test, so Databricks can attribute traffic from n8n in its audit logs and Query History. This required routing all API calls through a shared request helper. No functional changes to requests or node behavior; this is purely for traffic attribution.

item.title: Allow users to resize the review inbox sidebar
item.description: The workflow review inbox sidebar can now be resized by dragging its right edge, with a visible handle indicator while hovering or dragging. It defaults to 25% of the inbox width (clamped between 240–400px), can be resized between 240px and min(640px, 50%) of the available width, and remembers your chosen width proportionally across window resizes and navigation.

item.title: Airtop Node: Support running an agent with a specific browser profile
item.description: The Airtop node's Run an agent operation now supports selecting a specific Browser Profile ID, so agents can run against a saved browser profile instead of only the default. When set, the profile ID is sent to the agent; leaving it empty preserves the previous default behaviour. The existing session/extraction profile field has also been relabelled 'Browser Profile ID' for clarity, with no change to underlying parameters or API requests.

item.title: Edit Image Node: Add horizontal and vertical text alignment options
item.description: The Edit Image node's Add Image Text operation now includes Horizontal Alignment (Left/Center/Right) and Vertical Alignment (Top/Middle/Bottom) options, letting you reliably position text without manual trial-and-error on Position X/Y. Multiline text is centered per-line. Position X/Y now act as offsets relative to the chosen alignment. Available on node version 1.1+; existing workflows on version 1 keep the previous default (top-left) behavior.

item.title: G Suite Admin Node: Add "orgUnitPath" option to User create and update operations
item.description: The Google Workspace Admin node now supports an Organizational Unit field (orgUnitPath) on the User Create and Update operations, letting you assign an existing organizational unit to a user directly when creating or updating them. The organizational unit selector also now includes the root unit as an option.

item.title: Add Contact Support link to Help menu for Cloud instances
item.description: n8n Cloud instances now show a "Contact Support" item in the editor's Help menu, linking to support.n8n.io in a new tab. It appears between "Course" and "Report a bug" and is only visible on Cloud deployments, giving Cloud users quicker access to support resources. Self-hosted instances are unaffected.

item.title: Align workflow and agent header menus
item.description: The workflow and agent header menus have been aligned for consistency. The agent actions menu now sits next to the agent name, and version history has moved into that actions menu (disabled when no publish history exists). Both the workflow and agent menus now use the same dropdown component, with added icons and grouped items for a more consistent look. Existing import, export, favorite, and delete actions continue to work as before.

item.title: Add floating Markdown editor toolbar
item.description: The Markdown editor used for AI agent instructions now shows a floating formatting toolbar above selected text, instead of a toolbar that toggles between hidden and always visible. Selecting text reveals formatting options near the selection, and the toolbar disappears when the selection is cleared, giving a cleaner editing experience.

item.title: Rename n8n credits and n8n Connect copy to Gateway credits in the UI
item.description: The AI gateway feature's user-facing text has been renamed from "n8n credits"/"n8n Connect" to "Gateway credits" throughout the UI, including settings labels, credential pickers, tool connection tabs, and top-up messaging. The settings page moved from /settings/n8n-connect to /settings/gateway-credits, with old links automatically redirecting. This is a cosmetic rename only; underlying functionality is unchanged.

item.title: Update the order of providers in the agent builder model picker
item.description: The Agent Builder's model picker now orders providers to match the AI agent node's chat model picker: the currently selected provider appears first with a green 'Connected' checkmark, followed by n8n Connect-eligible providers grouped under an 'Included in n8n' header, then remaining providers, with aggregators like AWS Bedrock, OpenRouter, and Vercel AI Gateway listed last. A single divider separates the n8n Connect group from the rest, making it easier to find relevant providers.

item.title: Confluence Node: Add Page Get Comments operation
item.description: The Confluence node's Page resource now supports a Get Comments operation, listing footer comments on a page (one item per comment) via the Space + Page picker. It supports Return All/Limit with cursor pagination, Body Format (Storage, Atlas Doc Format, or Plain Text), and Sort By/Sort Direction options. Continue-on-fail is supported, and it returns no items for pages without comments.

item.title: MongoDB Node: Batch update and find-and-update writes with bulkWrite
item.description: The MongoDB node's Update and Find And Update operations now batch writes using bulkWrite instead of issuing one request per item, greatly speeding up large data ingests. This is available on new node version 1.5; existing workflows keep using their saved version, so behavior is unchanged unless you add a new MongoDB node. Output format and per-item results remain the same, but partial-failure scenarios (e.g. multi-collection or connection drop mid-write) may leave different write states than before.

item.title: Databricks Node: Add user-delegated OAuth2 credential (authorization code + PKCE)
item.description: The Databricks OAuth2 credential now supports user login via authorization code with PKCE, in addition to the existing service-principal client credentials flow, enabling per-user permissions and audit trails. Users can also customize OAuth scopes, with offline_access automatically preserved for token refresh on the user grant. Permission-denied errors now surface Databricks' own descriptive messages in executions, resource-locator dropdowns, and SQL failures, and trailing slashes in the configured host no longer break OAuth URLs. Existing service-principal credentials are unaffected.

item.title: Add adaptive layout to ChatInput
item.description: ChatInput now supports a new 'adaptive' layout that starts as a single compact row with an inline send/stop button and grows automatically as content is typed. It automatically falls back to the multiline layout if a custom button label or action slots are used, since adaptive only supports the default icon-only send/stop button.

item.title: Gotify Node: Add Gotify extra notification settings
item.description: The Gotify node now supports additional message options based on Gotify's msgextras spec: Click URL (opens a link when the notification is clicked), Big Image URL (displays an image in the notification), and Intent URL (Android-only action after delivery). These are optional fields added to the message creation options and are only included in the request payload when set.

item.title: Polish AI Assistant setup screen and connect modal
item.description: Refined the self-hosted AI Assistant setup experience: the setup screen now has a clearer title and offers "Get started" or "Set up later in Settings" on first visit, switching to "Turn off for this instance" on return visits. The connect modal hides its step-indicator dots when only one setup step remains, and connection test failures now show an additional sanitized "Error details" line to aid troubleshooting.

item.title: Add streaming to Message an Agent workflows
item.description: Message an Agent workflows now support opt-in response streaming, with output streamed live through Chat and Webhook triggers. Active tool and skill calls made by the agent are shown as capability pills in the UI, giving users real-time visibility into what the agent is doing while it responds.

item.title: Move AI Assistant connections from the sidebar to a "+" button in the text input
item.description: AI Assistant connections (MCP servers, Computer Use, Browser Use) have moved from the sidebar Connections card into a new "+" button menu next to the chat input. The menu shows connected, connecting, and disconnected statuses, flags unexpected disconnects with a red indicator, and lets users reconnect Computer Use or Browser Use directly. Wording changed from "Tools" to "Connectors"/"Services".

item.title: Show diff for closed review requests
item.description: Closed workflow reviews now show a Changes tab when approved, comparing the version published before approval against the approved version, with each side labeled by its publish state. If a review closed without approval, the Changes tab now explains that there's nothing to compare instead of hiding the tab.

item.title: Hide convert to sub-workflow when Execute Workflow nodes are excluded
item.description: When an n8n instance excludes the Execute Workflow node type via NODES_EXCLUDE, the convert-to-sub-workflow action is now hidden from the canvas context menu, selection toolbar, group title bar, and the Alt+X shortcut, since conversion requires that node. Additionally, workflow settings' 'This workflow can be called by' option is locked to 'No other workflows' in this case. Default n8n behavior is unaffected since these nodes aren't excluded by default.

item.title: Typeform Node: Allow custom OAuth2 scopes
item.description: The Typeform OAuth2 credential now supports custom scopes. By default it still requests the same three scopes needed by the Typeform Trigger node, but users can enable a 'Custom Scopes' toggle to edit the requested scope string and access additional Typeform API permissions. Custom scopes are now preserved when reconnecting the account instead of resetting to defaults.

item.title: Show review status as a badge on the workflows list
item.description: Workflows with an open review now show a status badge on the Overview workflows list, next to the publish and project indicators. The badge links to the review inbox when you're allowed to open it, otherwise it displays as plain text; a tooltip explains the decision status. Closed reviews no longer show a badge. The canvas 'Approved' banner has been removed, since publishing is now handled via the regular Publish button. Requires workflow reviews (enterprise feature).

item.title: Display success toast message on Browser Use connection
item.description: When connecting Browser Use automatically (via credential setup or the sidebar connect button), n8n now shows a success toast and closes the connect modal once your browser is connected. The connection modal was also streamlined: the external-link icon on the "Open Browser Use Extension" button was removed since it now opens in a popup, and the waiting-for-connection indicator was removed.

item.title: Microsoft SharePoint Node: Register version 2 and make it the default
item.description: The Microsoft SharePoint node now defaults to version 2, which is built on the Microsoft Graph API and supports OAuth2 or Entra service principal authentication with site/list resource locators. New SharePoint nodes added to workflows will use version 2 by default. Existing workflows using version 1 continue to run unchanged, as version 1 and its credentials remain fully supported.

item.title: Warn about self-escalation via Manage project roles scope
item.description: The custom instance role editor now warns when a role has only the Manage project roles permission, noting this lets a holder edit the scopes of any project-type custom role, including one they themselves hold, potentially self-escalating permissions. This joins existing warnings for Manage all roles and Members: Manage. No authorization behavior changed; this is a UI clarity improvement for admins managing custom roles under the Custom Roles enterprise feature.

item.title: Add stop execution button to the NDV
item.description: You can now stop a node's test-step execution directly from the NDV header, without closing the panel. A stop button appears next to Execute step while a node runs; it cancels the running execution, or cancels the test webhook wait if the run is waiting for an incoming webhook call. This also fixes a race where a stop click issued right after starting could be dropped.

item.title: Add Slack Agent view support
item.description: n8n Agents connected to Slack now use Slack's newer Agent view for direct messages by default when configuring a new Slack app, including threaded replies. Existing Slack integrations continue using the legacy Assistant view to avoid disrupting current setups. This is a behind-the-scenes messaging experience change with no configuration required for new connections.

item.title: Deprecate the "Any workflow" caller policy
item.description: The workflow setting "This workflow can be called by → Any workflow" is now deprecated ahead of removal in n8n v3, since it lets any project on the instance call a sub-workflow, bypassing project permissions. The workflow settings dropdown now labels it deprecated and shows a warning when selected, prompting a switch to another policy. MCP tool and public API descriptions were also updated to discourage new use of this value. No behavior or enum values change yet.

item.title: Add role-aware n8n credits top-up flow
item.description: The n8n credits top-up flow is now role- and subscription-aware. Cloud instance owners on a paid plan are taken directly to the Cloud Admin Panel to top up. Members and admins instead see a modal explaining that only the instance owner can top up, with a list of connected services. Trial users see a modal noting a paid plan is required, and trial owners get an upgrade option.

item.title: Anthropic Chat Model Node: Add prompt caching support
item.description: The Anthropic Chat Model node (v1.6) now supports opt-in prompt caching. New Options fields let you enable caching and set a cache TTL of 5 minutes or 1 hour, allowing the system prompt, tool definitions, and conversation history to be reused across requests, reducing cost and latency for agents with large prompts or many tool calls. Caching is disabled by default, and existing workflows on earlier node versions are unaffected.

item.title: Grist Node: Add upsert operation
item.description: The Grist node now supports a new Create or Update (upsert) operation, using Grist's built-in upsert API to create or update records in a single batched request. Users can define matching criteria fields, choose how to handle multiple matches (update first, none, or all), and populate fields via auto-mapping or manual definition, matching existing Create/Update UI patterns.

item.title: Show scopes for managed OAuth credentials with N8N_MANAGED_OAUTH_SHOW_SCOPES
item.description: Added a new environment variable, N8N_MANAGED_OAUTH_SHOW_SCOPES, allowing admins to specify managed OAuth credential types (e.g. googleOAuth2Api) that should still expose the scope field for customization, even when credentials are overwritten via environment variables. Previously, scope fields were always hidden for managed credentials with overwrites, breaking workflows that relied on customizing scopes.

item.title: Improve agent session tool call feedback
item.description: Agent session timelines now separate tool calls, approval requests, and approval responses into distinct events for clearer tracking. Preview chat shows expandable resolved tool call details and distinguishes declined approvals from failed calls. Dismissed MCP connection warnings now stay hidden for the rest of the current preview session, reducing repetitive alerts.

item.title: Simplify user flow for Browser Use connection
item.description: Connecting your browser to n8n's Browser Use AI Assistant is now simpler: clicking connect automatically opens the extension's connect view in a popup, which closes itself once connected. If the popup is closed or times out after 15 seconds, a Try again button lets you refocus it. The manual Open Browser Use extension button now also opens a popup instead of a new tab.

item.title: Adapt the OAuth consent screen for first-party clients
item.description: The OAuth consent screen now recognizes first-party clients, such as Form Trigger nodes using n8n login authentication. Instead of the generic third-party (MCP) layout, users see the form's icon, a tailored heading and description, and no trust checkbox or redirect-URI warning, letting them grant access immediately. Third-party MCP consent flows are unchanged.

item.title: Improve Browser Use connect conditions
item.description: Browser Use setup in the AI Assistant now better handles unsupported environments. On mobile and tablet devices, where browser extensions aren't possible, Browser Use and automatic credential setup are hidden entirely. On non-mobile devices with non-Chromium browsers, the option still appears but the connect modal now clearly explains that only Chrome or Chromium-based browsers, like Edge or Brave, are supported. Telemetry now also records browser support status to help track success rates.

item.title: Add preview chat to SessionTimeline view
item.description: Agent builder session views now include a preview chat you can dock beside the session timeline or open full screen, so you can inspect a trace and continue the conversation without switching pages. You can switch sessions and control the preview directly from the dock, open a preview in a new tab, start a new session from the agent list, and your preferred preview layout is remembered across the agent builder and session views.

item.title: Add snapshot option to every browser use interaction tool
item.description: Browser Use interaction tools (click, type, select, drag, hover, press, scroll, upload, dialog) now accept an optional snapshot parameter to return an accessibility snapshot directly in the response, either interactive or non-interactive. This removes the need for a separate snapshot call after each action, roughly halving the number of tool calls needed for browser automation.

item.title: Let users update review descriptions
item.description: When updating a workflow review with a newly pinned version, users can now edit the review description as part of the update flow. Review descriptions are preserved through the update, and are only visible to users with publish permission. The update dialog is more resilient to stale review state and description prefill failures.

item.title: MCP Server Trigger Node: Add server instructions option
item.description: The MCP Server Trigger node now has an optional Instructions field. Text entered here is sent to connecting MCP clients as part of the initialize response, letting you provide cross-tool guidance such as tool-choice rules or multi-step workflows that don't belong in any single tool's description. Clients that support this MCP feature (e.g. Claude Code) surface it in their system prompt automatically; others ignore it. The field defaults to empty, so existing workflows are unaffected.

item.title: Update NumberInput styling
item.description: The internal NumberInput design system component now visually matches the standard text input, with consistent sizing, borders, and focus/hover states, plus icon-based increment/decrement buttons with accessible labels and focus-to-select-all behavior. Currently this component is only used on the Agent Builder Settings page, affecting fields like Concurrency, Max iterations, Max uses, and Max parallel sub-agents.
